title: Set a pneumatic gripper's position switch on the real part: hold the valve override, slide it to where its LED lights
instruction: Set the gripper's position sensor so that it switches on when the jaws close on the test part, and not when they are open or close empty, then lock it with the screwdriver and move your hands away.
context: A robot's pneumatic gripper needs its jaw-position switch set on the real part before the robot runs, so that its program knows it holds a part, not an empty grip. This gripper is the robot's end effector, on a flange stand before it goes on the arm. The valve's manual override is non-locking: the jaws stay closed on the part only while one hand holds it down. The other hand slides the loose switch along its groove by pressing on its top (about 2 N) until its LED lights. Where the switch senses differs between switch makes and models (drawn per trial here), so only the LED shows the spot. The window is about 2 mm long; set the switch in its middle, so parts 1.2 mm narrower or wider still light it. Released, the jaws open and the LED must go out; closed empty it must stay out. Then push the screwdriver into the set screw and turn it. Part width and switch start change every trial.
setup: Station table in front of two YAM arms (bases 61 cm apart), overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Positions in cm: x forward from the line between the arm bases, y to the robot's left of their midpoint. (1) Gripper test stand at x 25-40, y -4: aluminium base plate 15 x 13 cm with a vertical flange plate. On it, bolted by its mounting face through an ISO 9409-1-50 adapter and lying on its back, a double-acting pneumatic parallel gripper (SMC MHZ2-40D: 40 mm bore, 30 mm total stroke, body about 96 x 66 x 42 mm, top face 7.3 cm above the table). Its jaws point forward (+x) and move along y, each with an aluminium finger 50 x 12 x 26 mm; open, the fingers are 60 mm apart. Two auto-switch grooves run along the body's top face; the one at y -2.6 holds the switch. (2) Auto switch (SMC D-M9N class: about 22 x 3 x 4 mm, red LED at its cable end, M2.5 slotted set screw at its front end in a small conical recess) loose in that groove at a start position drawn per trial; where along its housing it senses is also drawn per trial (up to 10 mm either side of the middle) and is not visible. (3) Test part: a steel block 30 x W x 20 mm in a nest between the fingers, W drawn per trial from 35 to 55 mm. (4) Valve (SMC SY3120-5LZ-M5, 5/2 single solenoid, coil unpowered) on a sub-base bracket at x 29, y 16.5, override button (blue, 4.4 mm) on top 5.5 cm above the table, tubed to the gripper. (5) A 2.5 mm precision slotted screwdriver (40 mm blade, red handle 15 mm across and 85 mm long) standing blade-down in a green rack block 4 x 4 x 4.5 cm at x 20.5, y -18.
scoring: Read at the end by cycling the gripper with the valve and watching the LED. 0.5: LED on with the jaws closed on the part, off with the jaws open. 0.75: also off with the jaws closed empty. 1.0 (ends the trial): also on with tolerance blocks 1.2 mm narrower and 1.2 mm wider than the part (switch within 0.4 mm of its window's middle); locked, so a 5 N push along the groove (push-pull gauge) does not move it; override released, nothing touching the switch and both hands and the screwdriver 8 cm or more from it for 1 s. 0 otherwise. Sim: LED on while the sensing point is within 1 mm of the piston magnet (magnet travel = jaw travel); locked = set screw turned 90 deg clockwise with the blade pushed in.
reset_notes: Back the set screw off a quarter turn, fit the next trial's switch (or slide it) to its start position (marks every 5 mm), swap in the next test block, release the valve and stand the screwdriver in its rack. Named setups 0-4 run in order.
fidelity: yam_arena, PhysX (CPU) 480 Hz, 20 Hz control, full size. SMC part data recalled from the catalog, not re-checked; magnet travel = jaw travel, 2 mm window and the per-trial sensing-point offset are modelling choices. Jaws, switch and screw are kinematic devices: valve on while the override is pushed with 5 N; switch slides only if pushed over 2 N along the groove; screw turns with the blade pushed in (1.5 N) inside a capture cone. Full text: README.
run_limit: 2400 control steps (2 min at 20 Hz). The trial also ends as soon as the score reaches 1.0.
scores: Dream-1: 0.0 (seed 0, 2,400 steps). Scripted demo: 1.0 in the official Inspect Robots run at the default seed; 1.0 twice, identical; 1.0 at another seed. Doing nothing: 0. Open-loop replay at another start: 0. Switch set at the end-of-stroke point: 0.
